core_question: Where and when will Level 4/5 autonomous driving achieve commercial viability at scale, and which business models (robotaxi, autonomous trucking, personal AV) will generate the highest returns?
central_thesis: The storyline should be led by the strongest public evidence, then translated into management choices.
narrative_focus: Evidence is densest around: timeline, funding
structure_logic: Open with the executive decision, show source-backed data exhibits, then move through business implications, risks and action gates.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Robotaxis will achieve commercial viability in dense urban areas by 2027, with unit economics breakeven at $0.50 per mile.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Determines whether to invest in robotaxi fleets vs. other AV applications.
needed_evidence: TCO breakdown for robotaxis (vehicle cost, sensors, maintenance, insurance, charging, remote ops) and revenue per mile from pilot programs.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Autonomous trucking will reach Level 4 on highways by 2026, reducing long-haul costs by 30%.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Guides investment in trucking automation vs. other segments.
needed_evidence: Pilot data on fuel savings, driver cost elimination, and accident rates; regulatory approvals for driverless trucks.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Consumer willingness to pay for Level 4 personal AVs will be less than $5,000, limiting adoption to luxury segments.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Impacts product strategy for OEMs considering AV options.
needed_evidence: Survey data on consumer willingness to pay, price elasticity, and feature valuation.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: China will lead in AV deployment by 2028 due to favorable regulation and high EV adoption, capturing 40% of global robotaxi miles.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Informs geographic allocation of R&D and partnerships.
needed_evidence: Regulatory timelines in China vs. US/EU, robotaxi pilot scale (Baidu, Pony.ai), EV penetration as proxy for AV readiness.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Lidar costs will drop below $500 per unit by 2026, enabling mass-market AV deployment.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Affects sensor strategy and supplier selection.
needed_evidence: Lidar pricing trends from manufacturers (Luminar, Hesai, Valeo), teardown reports, and volume forecasts.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Regulatory approval for driverless AVs without safety drivers will remain limited to 10 cities globally by 2027.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Constrains addressable market and scaling timeline.
needed_evidence: List of cities with driverless AV permits, regulatory frameworks (NHTSA, EU, China), and pace of new approvals.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Autonomous driving will reduce accident rates by 50% in early deployment areas, but public trust will remain low until 2030.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Affects marketing, insurance, and liability strategies.
needed_evidence: Accident data from Waymo, Cruise, and Tesla FSD; public opinion polls on AV safety.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Total addressable market = (Global vehicle miles traveled) * (AV penetration rate) * (revenue per mile)
variables: AV penetration rate (from adoption curve assumptions)
known_limitations: Penetration rate is highly uncertain; top-down can overestimate if adoption is slower.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Market size = Sum over segments (Number of AVs deployed * Average revenue per AV per year)
variables: Number of AVs by segment (robotaxi, trucking, personal) from company announcements and pilot data
Revenue per AV (subscription, per-mile, or purchase premium)
known_limitations: Requires granular data on deployments, which may be proprietary; scaling from pilots to mass market is uncertain.

variables: Funnel conversion rates from surveys and pilot data
known_limitations: Funnel rates are speculative; limited public data on conversion.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Value pool = (Cost savings from AV) + (New revenue from mobility services) - (Implementation costs)
variables: Cost savings (driver cost elimination, fuel efficiency, accident reduction)
known_limitations: Requires assumptions on cost curves and adoption; value may be double-counted.

charting_rule: Charts may use only evidence_ledger values, dates, source counts or same-unit comparable values tied to public URLs.
exhibit_narrative_rule: Every exhibit must be embedded in the section argument: prose sets up the management question before the exhibit and interprets the implication after it; never stack exhibits without prose.
